title: KV tile orchestration and soft-preempt paging spec
creator: Marco Chen
description: Goal: Design and prototype a paged/blocked KV cache implementation that minimizes tail latency and OOMs under oversubscription while preserving continuous batching throughput. This ticket captures the tile-oriented residency model, cooperative chunk leases, soft-preempt swap semantics, and GPU-friendly memory movement patterns. We need a spec that can be implemented as a runtime module and validated in trace-driven simulation and shadow deployments.
technical_design:
Overview:
- Represent KV cache as tiled "pages" (tile = contiguous KV entries aligned to GPU page size) instead of per-key fragments. Each tile has a small header with last-access epoch, lease owner id, residency score, and a compact refcount.
- Lease model: requests acquire cooperative leases on tiles for the duration of a batch window. Leases are soft (non-blocking) and can be preempted with a grace window to allow in-flight batches to complete.
- Paging primitives: host-staged staging buffers + pinned GPU DMA transfers where available. Swap uses DMA-friendly aligned chunk sizes to avoid small scatter-gather GPU copies.
- Residency budgets: per-GPU and per-model soft budgets; eviction uses epoch-decayed hotness + token-affinity boost when selection is ambiguous.
- Prefetch hints: router emits prediction hints (n-gram based and KV-usage-smoothed) at request enqueue time. Prefetch scheduler coalesces hints into tile-aligned DMA operations to maximize throughput.
- Continuous batching integration: batching scheduler groups requests while honoring lease acquisition to avoid head-of-line blocking. For requests that touch non-resident tiles, scheduler may spawn a short blocking batch to fetch tiles, then resume normal continuous batch flow.
- Graceful OOM fallback: when eviction cannot free memory in the grace window, requests are routed to compatible lower-memory model variants or host-only pipe with higher latency but preserved correctness.
- Observability: expose per-tile metrics (residency, lease churn, prefetch hit rate), per-batch latency breakdown (wait-for-prefetch, kernel-exec, serialization), and eviction latency histograms.
Implementation notes:
- Tile size trade-off: 64KB-512KB target; smaller tiles increase mapping granularity but raise metadata overhead. Start with 128KB and tune per-model.
- Metadata layout: keep headers in a compact host-side array with a GPU read-only snapshot for scheduling. Avoid per-access PCIe round-trips for metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Spec reviewed and accepted by runtime and infra leads
Prototype implements tile leasing, prefetch coalescing, and DMA-based swap in staging branch
Trace-driven simulator shows <5% tail-latency regression at 3x oversubscription compared to baseline and reduces OOMs by >=80% in synthetic hotset workloads
Observability hooks (tile metrics and batch breakdown) implemented and visible in staging console
Canary shadow rollout plan validated on one internal customer model with no impact to correctness
test_plan: Unit tests for lease state transitions, eviction selection, and prefetch coalescing logic
Simulator tests using production traces (recent 7-day sample) to validate eviction, prefetch hit rate, and memory churn
Microbench: GPU memory copy bandwidth measurement for aligned chunk sizes and various tile sizes on p4d and a100 clusters
End-to-end staging run with 24h soak under synthetic tail spikes and request-hotset churn
Canary shadow traffic for 48h against a non-critical model, compare token cost/latency and OOM counts
perf_targets: Median additional latency from prefetch path <= 1ms
95th percentile token generation latency regression <= 7% under 2x load
OOMs reduced by >=80% under worst-case hotset churn compared to existing slab allocator
Batch throughput (tokens/sec) within 5% of current runtime when resident ratio >= 60%
decisions: Use tile-aligned DMA transfers instead of fragmented host copies to reduce PCIe overhead
Lease model is cooperative/soft-preempt rather than strict locking to preserve batching throughput
Start with 128KB tile baseline, expose config by model to tune per-architecture
Eviction scoring combines LRU-ish epoch decay with token-affinity boost and size-normalization
open_questions: What is the safest default tile size for smaller models (e.g., 4B) to avoid wasting GPU memory?
How aggressive should grace window be before we trigger model fallback? 10ms, 50ms, or adaptive?
Should we let tenants opt into optimistic prefetch on private deployments where PCIe characteristics vary?
How to guarantee fairness when multiple tenants aggressively prefetch overlapping tiles?
risks: Too-large tiles increase eviction cost and may cause unnecessary DMA churn
Lease churn could reduce effective batching window if not tuned, hurting throughput
Incorrect prefetch heuristics can increase overall bandwidth and cause regressions rather than improvements
Edge-case races when swapping tiles back-to-back could cause briefly inconsistent KV reads if not zero-copy synchronized
implementation_notes: Implement metadata snapshot that is updated at batch boundaries to avoid per-request cache coherence traffic
Use lock-free ticketing for lease grants within a batch worker to avoid stalls
Provide a simulated DMA backend for developer laptops to test prefetch semantics without GPU hardware
Instrument costs (bytes moved, DMA ops, prefetch cancellations) to feed into future auto-tuning optimizer
rollout_plan: 1) Merge prototype behind runtime feature flag. 2) Run simulation validation and unit/perf tests. 3) Shadow canary with small internal models (48h). 4) Canary on selected customer models with opt-in. 5) Ramp to default as feature stabilizes and metrics meet SLOs. 6) Add auto-tuning to adjust tile size and grace windows based on observed telemetry.
